title: Why this, for her
question: Caplet asked this morning for every investing idea in the IPS to say how it is or isn't relevant to Laura. Six rooms checked the final for truth today; none asked whether its ideas land as reasons. Is there a place where an idea is named but not fused that a finance judge would mark down, and is there one repair worth offering tonight, or does it go to Caplet's own-words rewrite and the Final Report? (round 8 beat 8)
serves: North star 4 (investing knowledge applied, not name-dropped) and Caplet's top priority of 4 Nov (each idea's relevance to Laura); Wharton: Portfolio Analysis (effective use of investment concepts), Investment Strategy (why each choice belongs), Creativity and Presentation (Ray's 3 Nov note on AI-sounding phrasing)

rounds.name: Sealed positions, Jun's flaw hunt, Amara's registration
First blind read (three outside readers), Amara's scoring, replies by name
Second blind read of the merged lines and the two-word cut; the two sides check; the vote

essence: All six of us pointed at the same sentence: the final says it buys one bond per payment because that 'never needs rebalancing', which reads as our convenience, not a reason for Laura.

Six outside readers, in two blind tests, liked the version that says why ('so no cheque depends on what a bond sells for that January') best, but it never beat the final on the reason itself, because both Year 11 readers already found the why in the final.

So the only change Keel offers tonight is cutting two words, 'to us', which two of three readers flagged in both tests and nobody flagged once gone; the better reason, 'exactly' and the corny last line go on a card for Caplet's own rewrite.
decided: Flaw upheld 6-0: P3's 'which never needs rebalancing' names a convenience, not a reason for Laura
No repair beat the final in the first blind read (Felix's missed by one line: it cut the purchase date)
Second read 4-1-1; no merged line beat the final (Tess's G came closest: Q1 9 v 8, one short of +2; five of six picks)
Final vote (4), 6-0: offer only the ', to us,' cut tonight (493 strict); the reason, 'exactly' and the ending go on Caplet's card
seeds: Why does a ladder held to maturity need to reinvest anything? 3 of 3 second readers couldn't see it (the bonds pay interest years before the cheques start): card now, Final Report later
The closing tablet line was called the corny one in all 27 reader answers across both tests: Caplet's call
Readers prefer the 'no forced sale that January' paragraph more than it makes them understand the why: a Final Report sentence, with the risk the other method leaves open
